facts.statement: The genus Tribodus was described by Brito and Ferreira in 1989.
Tribodus lived during the mid Cretaceous period, specifically from the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: It lived during the mid Cretaceous (Albian-Cenomanian)

facts.statement: Fossils of Tribodus have been found in northern South America, North Africa, and southern Europe.
facts.quote: with fossils being known from northern South America, North Africa, and southern Europe

facts.statement: Tribodus is one of the few hybodonts known from articulated and nearly complete specimens.
facts.quote: making it one of the few hybodonts to be known from full body remains

facts.statement: The type species Tribodus limae grew to a total length of about 1 meter.
facts.quote: Tribodus limae reached a total length of about 1 m

facts.statement: Unlike other hybodonts, the lower jaw of Tribodus was short, did not reach the snout, and articulated with the upper jaw exclusively at the hyoid arch.
facts.quote: The lower jaw was relatively short and did not extend to the snout region and articulated with the upper jaw at exclusively at the hyoid arch unlike other hybodonts

facts.statement: Cartilage struts connected the upper and lower jaws of Tribodus, enhancing jaw strength.
facts.quote: with a number of cartilage struts connecting the upper and lower jaws which enhanced jaw strength

facts.statement: Tribodus possessed teeth specialized for durophagy, or eating hard-shelled organisms.
facts.quote: The teeth of Tribodus were specialised for durophagy (consuming hard shelled organisms)

facts.statement: Evidence of shrimp in stomach contents suggests that Tribodus was a benthic feeder.
facts.quote: It is suggested to have been a benthic feeder, with shrimp being discovered as stomach contents in some specimens

facts.statement: Species of Tribodus inhabited shallow marine, fluvial, and deltaic environments.
facts.quote: Species of Tribodus have been found in shallow marine as well as fluvial and deltaic environments

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Tribodus may have spawned in shallow-water vegetated areas.
facts.quote: It may have spawned in shallow-water vegetated areas

facts.statement: Historically, Tribodus was classified in the family Acrodontidae based on columnar osteodentine in its teeth.
facts.quote: Historically it has been asserted to be a member of the family Acrodontidae with other durophagous hybodonts, based on the presence of columnar osteodentine in its teeth

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest placing Tribodus in the family Distobatidae because its tooth morphology resembles members of that family.
facts.quote: However, other authors have suggested that it should instead be placed in the family Distobatidae due to the morphology of its teeth closely resembling members of that family

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Tribodus as Hybodontidae.
Tribodus lived from the Aptian to the Cenomanian, between 119.57 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Cenomanian (119.57 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Tribodus teeth were small, less than 5 mm across, and formed a flat grinding surface similar to living rays.
rejected.quote: They were small, less than 5 mm across and polygonal with a low cusp, and collectively formed a flat pavement that was effective at grinding
